manifest.name: tend: read novel branches by session, settle closed and superseded ones, and see open PRs

context.rationale:
A census of the four estate repos on 2026-09-30 applied tend's Branches tests and found 99 novel branches with no open pull request. tend sends every novel branch to you, but two readings it lacks settled 45 of them: 13 head a pull request closed without merging, 23 carry only commits pushed after their pull request merged, and 9 have most of their added lines on main already. It also reads branches one at a time, so a session whose work landed in one repo and stranded in another reads as unrelated rows, and it never looks at open pull requests: Branches excludes their branches and the Pull requests stream reads only merged ones, which left eleven drafts untouched for more than a month outside every stream. You approved this revision in outline in chat; the consent gate holds the wording until you have read it. Approve, approve with edits, or return it.

NO BRANCH DIFF FOR THIS: the gate holds the file uncommitted, so the item carries its whole patch. Read the patch pane.

items.title: skills/tend/SKILL.md
items.commentary: Branches gains a closed-tip class, proposed for deletion because the pull request keeps the commits and offers Restore branch. Every novel branch now gets two readings before it reaches you: only the commits after a merged pull request count, and the residue (added lines main lacks) is read against main, so a branch main has rewritten or retired is proposed for deletion rather than handed over. Novel branches are reported by session, reading closing states from state/sessions.json where the store is checked out; a session that closed Merged or Done with a novel branch comes first. Pull requests now reads open pull requests, reports those main already carries, and nominates stale ones for you to close.

+
+Read every novel branch before reporting it:
+
+- **After a merge.** If the branch heads a merged pull request, only the
+  commits after that pull request's `head.sha` are novel. Report those.
+- **Residue.** For each novel path, take the lines the branch added
+  (`git diff -U0 <merge-base> origin/<b> -- <path>`) and drop those present in
+  `git show origin/main:<path>`. What is left is the residue. Read it against
+  `main`.
+
+Report novel branches by session, not by branch. The `Claude-Session` trailer
+names the session, and one session's branches in several repos are one item.
+Where the session-record store is checked out (the checkout whose
+`.web-tools.json` declares `sessions`), `state/sessions.json` holds each
+session's branches and closing state. Name first a session that closed 🟣
+Merged or ⚫ Done with a novel branch: its record says the work is finished and
+the branch says it is not.
